title: Activation Protocols — Quickreference & Logbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational quickreference for activation (beta -> staged -> full) of product routes. It combines the minimal checklist teams need during a rollout with a short KPI watchlist and rapid-response runbook snippets. Intended for on-call, release lead, and PMs owning traffic gates.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API route launches and major model/service rollouts across Hosted and Dedicated.
- Not a replacement for full runbooks or SRE playbooks; use those for deep incident work.

Quick glossary:
- Activation: moving a feature/route from gated traffic to broader availability
- Probe: short test traffic pattern used to validate assumptions (latency, correctness, cost)
- Canary: incremental traffic ramp applied to a slice of users

Preflight (T - 48 to T - 2 hours):
- Confirm canary config in Console: route, model pin, rollout window, max shard size. (owner: release lead)
- Smoke tests: run synthetic probes (5 samples, 99% success) against canary endpoint.
- Cost sanity: compare expected token cost delta vs baseline (goal: delta < 12%).
- Capacity check: Dedicated pool headroom >= 30% for peak window.
- Alerting: ensure token-level cost alert, P95 latency, error-rate and fallback alerts are enabled (channels: #prod-ops, #oncall).
- Stakeholder notify: product, eng SRE, support paged with ETA and rollback window.

Canary Phasing (default cadence):
- Phase 0: synthetic probes only (0% user traffic) — 15m observation.
- Phase 1: 1% real users — 30m.
- Phase 2: 5% real users — 45m.
- Phase 3: 15% real users — 60m.
- Phase 4: 50% real users — 90m.
- Phase 5: 100% after final check — manual gate.
Notes: adjust timing for traffic shape or weekly patterns; for high-risk launches add additional hold windows.

KPI Watchlist (quick thresholds) — primary signals:
- P50 latency (text-gen): target < 80ms; yellow >= 80ms and < 150ms; red >= 150ms.
- P95 latency: target < 250ms; yellow 250–500ms; red > 500ms.
- Error rate (5m window): target < 0.5%; yellow 0.5–2%; red > 2%.
- Successful tokens per second (throughput): target >= baseline * 0.9; red if < baseline * 0.7.
- Cost per 1k tokens (estimated runtime): deviation +/−12% allowed; alert if > +25%.
- User-visible correctness (sampled evals): pass rate >= 97%; red if < 94%.
Quick sanity matrix example:
- Green: P95 < 250ms, error < 0.5%, cost delta < 12% -> proceed to next phase
- Yellow: 250ms < P95 < 500ms or error 0.5–2% -> hold phase for additional 1.5x observation, run focused traces
- Red: P95 > 500ms or error > 2% or cost delta > +25% -> rollback to previous stable model/version

Runbook snippets (fast actions):
1) If P95 spikes above 500ms during a phase:
  - Immediately flip canary traffic to synthetic-only (Console: set phase to 0%).
  - Posttrace: capture 3 full traces at the spike timestamps; tag with label "canary-spike-<phase>".
  - Oncall: page #oncall and create JIRA PRODOPS-INC with short description and traces attached.
  - If root cause appears to be model (OOM, kernel error): rollback to model X (use pinned previous).
2) If error rate > 2% and errors are 5xx from runtime: 
  - Switch route to fallback policy (route-level config) -> lightweight model or cached response path.
  - Notify customer-success for impacted customers in the window.
  - Re-run 10 targeted synthetic probes across regions.
3) If cost delta > +25%:
  - Pause ramp and limit sampling to 0.5% while finance and release lead triage.
  - Check batching/sequence-length misconfig (are clients sending much longer contexts?).
  - If client behavior change, coordinate opt-out or throttle with partner.

Rollback criteria (fast-check):
- Any RED in KPI watchlist sustained for > 5 minutes OR
- A spike correlated with increased user-facing errors (support tickets x10 baseline in 30m) OR
- Significant capacity exhaustion (Dedicated headroom < 10%)
Rollback steps (short):
1) Set canary to 0% user traffic.
2) Re-pin route to previous model version and verify smoke tests.
3) Announce rollback to stakeholders with short impact note and next steps.

Communication & post-decision logbook (template snippet):
- Time: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- Phase when decision made: Phase #
- Trigger: e.g., P95=620ms; errors=3.1%
- Action taken: rollback to v1.3.2; canary -> 0%
- Owners involved: Release lead (name), Oncall (name), PM (name), Support rep (name)
- Follow-ups: RCA owner, timeline for next attempt

Short checklist for final go/no-go at 100% gate:
- Last 3 phases stable and green for > 1.5x observation window
- No emergent support tickets with severity P0/P1 in last 60m
- Capacity: Dedicated pool headroom >= 20% (or autoscale validated)
- Cost delta reviewed and flagged acceptable by finance/product
- Rollback plan verified and stakeholders reachable for the next 2 hours

Owner roster (on-call rotation snapshot):
- Release lead: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Oncall SRE: Diego Martinez (diego@redwood.ai)
- Product PM: Fiona Chen (fiona@redwood.ai)
- Support lead: Evelyn Brooks (evelyn@redwood.ai)

Post-launch checks (T + 1h, T + 6h, T + 24h):
- T+1h: quick stability sweep (alerts cleared, P95 within expected)
- T+6h: business metrics sanity (error volume, adoption signals), collect 100 sampled outputs for qualitative check
- T+24h: cost delta check, initial RCA notes if anomalies, schedule stakeholder debrief

Notes / prompts to self (rough brainstorm):
- Consider adding a short automatic canary rollback when P95 > 600ms for 3 continuous minutes (tunable).
- We should add a small synthetic test that exercises long context edge-cases preflight.
- Investigate a compact "launch card" view in Console showing the quick KPIs and buttons for hold/rollback.

Appendix — quick CLI snippets (ops):
- set canary 0%: rcli rollout set --route <route> --canary 0 --note "auto-hold"
- capture traces: rcli trace export --route <route> --from <t-5m> --to <t> --label canary-spike
- pin route to old model: rcli route update --route <route> --model "model:v1.3.2" --pin true

End of logbook entry. Keep this doc short and in-sync with product-ops runbooks. If anything is unclear, flag during next triage meeting.
